newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BROWN PRAISES NEW SCOTTISH STRIKE FORCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BROWN PRAISES NEW SCOTTISH STRIKE FORCE.

text.p: Scotland coach Craig Brown believes he may at long last have unearthed a striking partnership to follow in the footsteps of Ally McCoist and Maurice Johnston.

Brown says Blackburn forward Kevin Gallacher, who scored both goals in their 2-0 win over Austria on Wednesday, and his striking partner Darren Jackson, can play a key role in Scotland's progress towards the World Cup finals in France in 1998.
Their mutual understanding on Wednesday night recalled McCoist and Johnston, who scored the bulk of the goals which booked Scotland's passage to the World Cup in Italy seven years ago.
"The partnership of Gallacher and Jackson is very similar to the one that Mo and Ally had," Brown said.

"Both Ally and Mo had strength and pace which caused major problems throughout the world and their record together was as good as anyone's. Ally still has strength but he would admit himself he is not as quick as he used to be."
"Both Jackson and Gallacher are quick and full of running and if they see grass they will knock the ball into it and go."

But Brown insisted that despite Jackson and Gallacher's performances, the door was not closed on Everton's aerial threat of Duncan Ferguson, who withdrew from the squad for Wednesday's match with injury.
"Traditionally we've always tried had a big man-wee (little) man partnership up front but that is not now our only option," Brown said.
"However, I have to make it clear we have not discounted Duncan Ferguson from our plans. We can't shut anyone out."
"But it is now very hard to leave out either Jackson or Gallacher after the way they played against the Austrians."
Wednesday's result left Scotland seven points clear of second-placed Austria in European qualifying group four although the Austrians have two matches in hand.
The Scots have not conceded a goal in their six matches to date.
